subject.title: feat(memory): graduate sessionMemory from experimental — solve the multi-session continuity problem

question: Should OpenClaw graduate session transcript memory from experimental, and should it become default-on for new installs or remain stable opt-in until the privacy/source-policy blockers are closed?
rationale: The code path exists, but changing the stability/default contract affects transcript privacy, cross-channel visibility, QMD export behavior, embedding cost, and upgrade expectations.

options.title: Layer Stable Opt-In First
options.body: Keep transcript memory opt-in while maintainers close source-label, visibility, duplicate-indexing, ranking, privacy, and cost-documentation criteria, then revisit default-on separately.

options.title: Default On After Privacy Gates
options.body: Sponsor a broader product change that makes session transcript memory default-on only after DM/group scope, QMD export, opt-out, and upgrade behavior are documented and tested.

options.title: Keep Experimental
options.body: Leave the experimental flag and current docs in place until live evidence and user demand justify a new stability contract.

recommendation.title: Layer Stable Opt-In First
recommendation.body: Keep transcript memory opt-in while maintainers close source-label, visibility, duplicate-indexing, ranking, privacy, and cost-documentation criteria, then revisit default-on separately.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the experimental feature and are the strongest history-backed routing candidate for the stability/default contract decision.
